newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut magistrate demands death for former warlord.
newsitem.headline: Beirut magistrate demands death for former warlord.

text.p: A Beirut magistrate on Wednesday demanded the death penalty for jailed former Christian warlord Samir Geagea and two followers on charges of murdering prime minister Rashid Karami in 1987.
It was the fifth murder case brought against Geagea, who is already serving two life sentences for previous murder convictions and a lengthy jail term for a third.

Magistrate George Ghantous issued an indictment demanding the death penalty for Geagea for ordering Karami's killing, and for two top security officials of Geagea's Lebanese Forces (LF) group -- both of whom are at large -- for planning the murder.
Ghantous also demanded life jail terms for 13 LF members and a Lebanese army brigadier for involvement in Karami's killing.
A remote-controlled bomb blew up Karami's helicopter off the Lebanese coast in June 1987 during the 1975-90 civil war.
Geagea and the remaining defendants -- of whom 11 are at large -- will be tried by Lebanon's highest court, the Judicial Council. No date has been set for the trial.

Geagea, the first of the civil war chieftains to stand trial, is serving a life sentence for masterminding the 1990 killing of Christian rival Dani Chamoun and members of his family and the murder in the same year of a former LF member.

Geagea, whose LF was outlawed three years ago, was acquitted last year of a 1994 church bombing that killed 11 people, but was sentenced to 10 years' jail for establishing a military faction after the goverment disbanded all militias in 1991.
In December, the Judicial Council opened Geagea's trial on charges of ordering a 1991 attempt on the life of a government minister.

The government has ordered a general amnesty for crimes committed during the civil war but postwar crimes and certain high-profile killings like Karami's assassination which had already been referred to the Judicial Council were excluded.
